content.text:
Reworked the submit fix and rebuilt the plugin.

## What changed

My first fix wrote `body` + `\r` **back-to-back in the same tick** — and that's the trap: Claude Code reads a fast input burst as a *paste*, where a trailing `\r` becomes a literal newline, not a submit. So the prompt still didn't run.

The new approach **defers the Enter to the next timer tick** (`deliver_pending_inputs` runs every ~1s):
- Tick N: type the body (newline stripped), queue the pane on `pending_submit`.
- Tick N+1: send a lone `\r` to that pane — arriving ~1s after the paste settled, so Claude Code sees a real Enter and runs the prompt.

Plugin compiles + clippy-clean on wasm, and I rebuilt the **release** wasm (now 20:17) — that's the artifact the cockpit loads.

## To actually test it

The running cockpit has the **old** plugin baked in — Zellij doesn't hot-reload a plugin in a live session. You need a fresh session with the new wasm:

```
just refresh        # from a plain shell, outside Zellij
```

(If `just refresh` still exits non-zero, `just up` does the same launch without the kill steps — and paste me the error lines if either fails; per the last round, the build/config/layout are all clean, so any failure is in the zellij launch itself.)

Then spawn an agent with a prompt and watch: the text should type in, then **~1 second later submit on its own**.

If it *still* doesn't submit after loading this build, the remaining suspect is that `write_chars_to_pane_id` wraps output in bracketed-paste (making even a lone `\r` literal) — in which case we'd need a different key-send mechanism. But a separated, standalone CR is the standard fix and should do it. Want me to fold this into the commit stack now, or hold until you've confirmed it live?

that works.  now: how do sub-agent results get back to the spawning agent?

soloterm analysis:

 Solo has no return-value channel — results come back out-of-band
  A Solo sub-agent is a PTY-backed terminal session, not a function call. spawn_agent hands you a
  process_id, you prompt it with send_input, and from then on the child and parent are two independent
  conversations. There is no result = await child(...). Results get back to the spawner through three
  separate mechanisms that you compose yourself:
  1. Reading the child's terminal output (the raw channel)
  The parent scrapes the child's PTY:
  - get_process_output(process_id, lines=N) — recent rendered terminal rows
  - get_process_raw_output — raw bytes
  - search_output / search_raw_output — find a sentinel in the scrollback
  This is brittle for structured data (you're parsing a terminal), so it's mostly used to confirm progress
  or grep for a marker the child was told to print (e.g. ROUND 3 READY in Solo's own worked example).
  2. Shared coordination primitives (the real result hand-off)
  The durable pattern is: the child writes its result into shared state, the parent reads it. Solo's
  coordination plane gives you:
  - Scratchpads — the canonical "hand back a findings/plan/report" channel. Parent tells the child in its
  prompt "write your result to scratchpad X"; child calls scratchpad_write/scratchpad_append; parent reads
  it with scratchpad_read. Revision guards (expected_revision) prevent clobbering.
  - Todos — when the result is task-shaped (ownership, status, comments).
  - Locks — mutual exclusion around shared edits.
  - (KV exists in the model but is disabled in this Solo instance.)

  So the actual "return value" is a scratchpad id agreed on up front, not a tool response.

  3. Knowing when the result is ready (synchronization)

  There's no blocking await. The parent doesn't poll — it arms an idle-triggered timer:
  - timer_fire_when_idle_any(processes, max_wait_ms, body) — wake me when any watched child goes idle (i.e.  finished its turn)
  - timer_fire_when_idle_all([...], max_wait_ms, body) — wake me when all of them are idle

  When the timer fires, body is injected into the parent's conversation as a fresh user turn. That body is   where you put the "now go read scratchpad X / get_process_output on pid N" instruction. So the loop is:

  spawn_agent → send_input(prompt: "...do work, write result to scratchpad 42")
              → timer_fire_when_idle_any([child_pid], 600000,
                   "child idle: read scratchpad 42, then continue")
     (parent suspends; on wake it reads the scratchpad / output)

  The shape of it

  Spawn returns a handle, not a future. The child pushes its result into a shared store (scratchpad/todo)   or its terminal; the parent is woken by an idle timer and pulls the result back. Coupling is by
  convention — both sides have to agree on the scratchpad id or output marker in advance.

content.text:
Confirmed. Here's how it maps — panopt covers Solo's three mechanisms unevenly:

**Like Solo, `spawn_agent` returns a handle (`process_id`), not a future.** There's no `result = await child(…)`. Results come back out-of-band, and panopt's coverage is:

| Solo mechanism | panopt status |
|---|---|
| **#2 shared-state hand-off** (scratchpads/todos/locks) | ✅ **Fully present** — `note_*` (panopt's scratchpads), `todo_*`, `lock_*`. This is the real result channel. |
| **#1 PTY output scrape** (`get_process_output`/`search_output`) | ❌ **No MCP tool.** The plugin reads pane scrollback for status (#142) but never exposes it to an orchestrator. Brittle anyway — notes are strictly better. |
| **#3 synchronization** (idle timer wake) | ⚠️ **Half.** The daemon *tracks* child idle-state — `process_get` returns `agent_state` (idle/thinking/planning), `agent_list` returns `idle_seconds` — so the parent can *know* when a child finished, but there's **no blocking await**; the parent must poll. |

### What works today (no code)

The note/todo hand-off, exactly Solo's durable pattern — agree the channel up front:

```
#N = note_create(title: "weather result")          # the agreed return slot
spawn_agent(prompt: "check weather in Portland OR; note_append your result to
                     note #N; then stop")
# synchronize: poll process_get(child_id) until agent_state == "idle"
#   (more robust: give the child a todo and watch for todo_complete, or have it
#    append a "DONE" sentinel — "idle" only means it finished a turn, not the task)
note_read(#N)                                        # pull the result back
```

So the "return value" is **a note (or todo) id agreed in advance**, never a tool response — same as Solo.

### The one real gap: clean synchronization

Everything works except *waiting*. The parent has to poll `process_get`/`todo_get` in a loop, which burns turns and is easy for the model to abandon. Solo solves this with an idle-fire timer that injects a fresh user turn; Claude Code can't have a turn injected, but it **can** block on a tool call — so panopt's natural equivalent is a **blocking `wait_for_idle(process_ids, timeout_ms)`** that long-polls the `agent_state` the daemon already tracks and returns when the child(ren) go idle (or times out). Then:

```
wait_for_idle([child_id], 600000)   # blocks, no turn-burning poll loop
note_read(#N)
```

(Caveat to verify: a multi-minute MCP call vs the proxy's HTTP reconnect budget — may need a modest cap with parent re-call, or a proxy tweak.)

This is squarely related to the cleanup-model work (#190 line). How far do you want to take it?

# Shipped agent-type profiles.
#
# Each top-level table is one `tool_type` - the string an `agent_tools` row
# stores to say what kind of agent a config launches. This file is compiled
# into the binary (`include_str!`) and is the authoritative default set; a user
# override at `<config-dir>/panopt/agent-types.toml` is merged on top (scalars
# override, maps merge by inner key, lists replace wholesale). See
# `panopt-core::agent_profiles` for the merge rule, the placeholder set, and
# load-time validation.
#
# A profile is pure data driving generic interpreters: `spawn` is a template the
# spawn interpreter renders into a concrete (argv, env, files) launch; `status`
# is regexes the status interpreter matches against the agent's output. There is
# no per-type code - adding an agent type that fits this shape is a new table
# here (or in the override), not a code change.

[claude-code]
display_name = "Claude Code"

# Bootstrap text returned as `agent_instructions` from `spawn_agent` (#159). An
# orchestrator prepends this to the spawned child's first prompt so it knows its
# own panopt identity and how to coordinate. Rendered by the daemon at spawn time
# against the known facts (no `{{file:...}}` here - the daemon writes no files).
# The child already has the panopt MCP tools wired via its launch config, so this
# is about identity and etiquette, not connection.
instructions = '''
You are a panopt-managed agent. Your instance is process #{{process_id}}, named "{{name}}" (stable id `{{agent_id}}`) in workspace {{ws}}.

You already have the panopt MCP tools available. To coordinate:
- Call `identify` (or `whoami`) to register your presence under `{{agent_id}}`.
- Use `process_report` to report your status as you work.
- Use todos, notes, and locks to coordinate with the other agents in this project.
'''

[claude-code.spawn]
# Launch claude with a generated stdio MCP config that boots `panopt _mcp-proxy`.
# The proxy holds the long-lived MCP session and forwards to panoptd over HTTP,
# so the session survives daemon restarts. This mirrors the cockpit's
# hand-built launch (crates/panopt/src/mcp.rs) - except panopt renders the
# `{{...}}` placeholders itself rather than leaning on claude's own `${VAR}`
# expansion, which is what lets the same engine launch agents that don't expand
# env vars.
# `--disallowedTools Agent` removes Claude Code's built-in sub-agent (Agent/Task)
# tool from the model's context entirely, and `--append-system-prompt` points at
# the tool that is available, so a spawned agent that is itself asked to "spawn an
# agent" reaches for panopt's `spawn_agent` rather than its own built-in tool
# (todo #190 follow-up). MCP tools (spawn_agent et al.) are unaffected. Keep this
# text in sync with `SPAWN_DIRECTIVE` in crates/panopt/src/agent.rs.
argv = [
    "claude",
    "--mcp-config", "{{file:mcp_config}}",
    "--disallowedTools", "Agent",
    "--append-system-prompt", "To spawn, launch, run, or delegate to an agent in this project, use the panopt `spawn_agent` MCP tool, then `send_input` to task it. The built-in sub-agent (Agent/Task) tool is intentionally unavailable: every agent must be a first-class panopt pane so it joins the shared coordination plane (registry, todos, notes, locks).",
]

# Rendered to a temp file at spawn; its path replaces `{{file:mcp_config}}` in
# argv. A multi-line TOML literal string ('''...''') holds the JSON verbatim.

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "panopt": {

        "_mcp-proxy",

}

Done with the doc layer + memory. Here's the build plan for the two pending tools (full parity):

### `wait_for_idle` — clean, no plugin (build first)
- **Args:** `{ process_ids: [u64], timeout_ms, mode: "all" | "any" }`.
- **Wiring:** `WaitForIdleArgs` in params.rs → `TOOL_SURFACE` entry → `Tool` enum variant → `dispatch_local` arm (the `tool_enum_covers_tool_surface` test enforces this).
- **Handler:** async poll loop — each iteration acquires the state Mutex *only* for a quick `agent_state` check, **releases before `sleep`** (never hold the lock across `await`), returns when the all/any-idle (or terminal: stopped/exited) condition is met or on timeout.
- **Proxy caveat → design choice:** `panopt _mcp-proxy` forwards over HTTP with a reconnect budget; rather than risk a multi-minute held connection, **cap each call ~60–120s** and return a `timed_out` + still-busy list the parent re-calls on. Avoids proxy fragility entirely.

### `process_output` / `search_output` — needs plugin plumbing (build second)

## panopt
PANopt coordination daemon: shared todos and notes across agents.
Each connection is scoped to one project by the ?ws=<project path> query parameter on the server URL.
- Registry: call identify (name, optional status) on startup so others can see you; whoami returns your own entry; agent_list returns every agent on the project (each entry's key_source is `declared` for stable `?agent=<id>` ids or `session` for the rotating MCP session id - only session entries idle-prune). Connecting already registers you. agent_leave removes your registry entry and releases your locks; the idle sweep handles agents that just disappear.
- Locks: lock_acquire (name, optional note) takes a named advisory lock and is non-blocking; lock_release frees it; lock_status lists every held lock. Locks are advisory - agents cooperate, the daemon does not enforce.
- Todos: todo_create (returns an id), todo_list (summaries), todo_get (one todo in full), todo_update (edit any field), todo_complete, todo_delete, todo_add_blocker / todo_remove_blocker / todo_set_blockers, todo_comment_add / todo_comment_update / todo_comment_delete, todo_tags_list (project tag vocabulary, union with notes), and todo_lock / todo_unlock (advisory `todo:<id>` lock, surfaced as locked_by on todo_get). Each todo also projects to .panopt/todos/<id>.md.
- Notes: note_create (returns an id), note_list, note_get (one note in full), note_append (add to body), note_read (body only), note_update (replace title, body, and/or tags), note_delete, note_tags_list (project tag vocabulary, same union as todo_tags_list). Each note also projects to .panopt/note/<id>.md.
- Agent tools (config layer): agent_tool_create (returns an id), agent_tool_list, agent_tool_get, agent_tool_update, agent_tool_delete. Durable per-project agent configurations the cockpit can spawn from. Projected to .panopt/agent_tools.md.
- Processes (instance layer): process_create (kind agent/command/terminal, optional agent_tool_id, returns an id), process_list, process_get, process_update, process_delete. Per-p… [truncated]

content.text:
Short answer: **functionally yes, with two deliberate scoping gaps — but it's code-complete, not yet *proven* (live verification #208 is still open).** Let me be precise against Solo's three mechanisms:

| Solo | panopt | Parity |
|---|---|---|
| **#2 shared-state** — scratchpads / todos / locks | `note_*`, `todo_*`, `lock_*` | ✅ Full |
| **#3 sync** — `timer_fire_when_idle_any/all` | `wait_for_idle(process_ids, timeout_ms, mode=all\|any)` | ✅ Functional — *different mechanism* (see below) |
| **#1 output scrape** — `get_process_output` + `search_output` + **raw** variants | `process_output` + `search_output` (rendered rows only) | ⚠️ Partial — no raw-bytes variants |

### The two honest gaps

1. **No raw-output channel.** Solo has `get_process_raw_output` / `search_raw_output`; panopt only serves *rendered* rows (the plugin's `get_pane_scrollback` gives rendered viewport, not raw bytes). Rarely what you want, but it's a real difference.
2. **`wait_for_idle` is blocking, not a callback.** Solo's timer injects a fresh user turn when the child idles; Claude Code can't have a turn injected, so panopt *blocks and returns* instead — same effect for the await pattern, but capped at 120s (re-call on `timed_out`) rather than an open-ended timer.

Plus the inherent capture caveats panopt shares with any terminal scrape (and the docs say so): output is ~1s-lagged, a window only (last 300 viewport rows), and only for agents the cockpit is observing.

### The important caveat

**It's code-complete and committed (`2574a15`), passing build/clippy/tests — but the runtime behavior is *not yet verified live*** (that's exactly todo **#208**). Unit tests can't exercise a blocking poll over real `agent_state` or actual pane capture. So until you `just refresh` and run a real spawn-and-await, "done" means *the code is written*, not *proven working*.

If you want certainty, #208 is quick: spawn a child with "write your result to note #N", `wait_for_idle([child])`, then `note_read(#N)` — that one loop exercises all three mechanisms end to end. Want me to walk through it once you've refreshed?

Confirmed both root causes. This wasn't intentional checking — the orchestrator was working around **two real timing bugs** in the freshly-shipped code:

## Bug 1 — the opening prompt was delivered too early (and lost)

`process.rs:293` reports the pid **before** `exec`-ing claude, so the row flips to `running` the instant the shim starts — *seconds before* Claude Code's TUI is actually up. The plugin delivers queued input the moment it sees `running`, so it typed the opening prompt into a pane that wasn't ready to receive it → lost. Worse, it then marks the input delivered and acks it, so **there's no retry** — which is exactly why you had to `send_input` the task manually.

## Bug 2 — `wait_for_idle` returned on a stale "idle"

`wait_for_idle` treats `agent_state == "idle"` as done. But a *just-booted* agent sitting at its empty prompt is also classified "idle." So the first wait returned immediately ("finished its turn") when the agent hadn't started — your "earlier idle reading was stale." Right after spawn, idle means *hasn't begun*, not *done*.

Both come from the same gap: nothing distinguishes "ready / has picked up its task" from "running / booted."

## Fixes

1. **Delivery readiness gate** (fixes #1): deliver queued input only once the agent is *ready*, not merely `running`. The plugin's `ProcessRow` already carries `agent_state`, so gate on `running && agent_state.is_some()` — i.e. wait until the status observer has actually classified the pane (TUI rendered) before typing into it. Cheap, plugin-only.

2. **`wait_for_idle` ignores not-yet-tasked agents** (fixes #2): a process isn't "settled" while it still has **undelivered queued input** (its task hasn't even been typed). Combined with #1 the flow becomes clean: spawn → prompt pending → wait sees pending, keeps waiting → prompt delivers when ready → agent goes busy → finishes idle, pending cleared → settled. (Optional further hardening: also require the agent to have been seen *busy* during the wait, to close the sub-second window between delivery and the agent reacting.)

Neither is large — #1 is a one-line gate in `deliver_pending_inputs`; #2 adds a pending-input check in the `wait_for_idle` handler loop (the daemon can already enumerate pending inputs).

Want me to implement both now (and re-verify via the same weather spawn)? I'd also fold a note into todo #208 so the verification criteria capture these. Or if you'd rather, I can file them as their own bug todos first.

Both timing fixes are in and pushed (`5ce5bdb`) — they want the same live re-verify as #208 (spawn weather again; the prompt should land on its own and the first `wait_for_idle` should *not* return until the agent actually works).

## On the orphan config — best policy

That's the ad-hoc-config accretion I flagged as cleanup **B (todo #205)**. What happened: an ad-hoc `spawn_agent` (no `agent_tool_id`) mints a **config** *and* a **process**; you deleted the process, but the config it created persists and clutters `agent_tool_list`.

The right model is Solo's: **ad-hoc = disposable, declared = durable.** Three ways to get there:

1. **Ephemeral flag, reaped with its last instance (recommended — this is #205).** Mark spawn-created configs `ephemeral`; when the last live instance of an ephemeral config is deleted, soft-delete the config too. Configs you make explicitly (`agent_tool_create` / the cockpit form) are durable templates and never auto-reaped. Keeps per-instance config identity (own system_prompt/args) *and* self-cleans. Matches Solo's command-vs-agent split exactly.

2. **One shared ad-hoc config per `tool_type`.** All ad-hoc spawns point at a single `claude-code (ad-hoc)` config; nothing to clean (the singleton persists harmlessly). Simpler, but the config list shows a generic shared row and you lose per-spawn config differentiation (instances still get their own name/extra_args, just not their own config).

3. **No config at all for ad-hoc spawns (deeper).** Let a process carry its `tool_type`/spec inline so an ad-hoc spawn needs no `agent_tool` row. Cleanest conceptually — closest to Solo, where ad-hoc agents simply aren't config entries — but a bigger change, since the edge resolves the profile via `process.agent_tool_id` today.

I'd go with **#1** — it's the best balance (auto-clean + keeps per-instance identity) and it's already the plan in #205. Until it's built, the interim is just deleting the orphan with `agent_tool_delete` (or I can add a line to the disposal etiquette telling orchestrators that an ad-hoc spawn leaves a config to delete too).

Want me to implement **#205** now (ephemeral flag + reap-on-last-instance, with the V17 migration)? That'd close this for good — and it unblocks **#206** (the idle-TTL sweep) right after.

`spawn_agent` returns a handle (`process_id`), not a future — results come back out-of-band, same as Solo. On 2026-06-07 the user chose **full Solo parity** for the three return mechanisms.

**Status / how to apply:**
- **#2 shared-state hand-off (DONE, works today):** notes (= Solo scratchpads) + todos + locks already exist. The pattern — agree a note/todo id up front, child writes result there before stopping, parent reads it — is now documented in the daemon server `instructions` (handler.rs get_info orchestration bullet) and the `[claude-code]` bootstrap `instructions` (defaults.toml: child writes its result to the named note/todo before finishing).

Settled = agent_state "idle" OR terminal status (stopped/exited) OR gone. Capped at 120s (default 60s); returns `{idle, timed_out, mode, processes:[{process_id,agent_state,status,settled}]}` so the parent re-calls on timeout. # Plan: 1:1 → 1:N agent factory model (todo #190)

## Context

Todo #190 asks us to adopt Solo's two-layer agent model in panopt: an **agent tool**
is a reusable runtime *template* (id, name, command, tool_type, enabled), and an
**agent process** is a running *instance* spawned from a template — one template, many
concurrent instances. Spawning should be a factory call.

**What exploration found:** panopt has *already built* ~90% of this. The V6 migration
split the old `roster` into `agent_tools` (template) + `processes` (instance); the
schema already supports 1:N (nullable `agent_tool_id` FK, no unique constraint);
`spawn_agent` / `send_input` / `extra_args` / bootstrap `instructions` are all wired,
and the MCP tool names already match Solo (`agent_tool_list`, `spawn_agent`,
`send_input`). So this is **not** a build-out — it's removing the last 1:1 constraint
and fixing a latent collision it was masking.

Two things keep the model at 1:1 today:

1. **A single 1:1 guard** in `process_start_with` (state.rs:1303-1314) returns the
   existing live instance instead of spawning a second. `spawn_agent` is a thin alias
   over `process_start`, so both inherit the guard (DESIGN S10).
2. **A latent identity collision**: the edge derives each instance's `agent_id` from
   `config.name` (process.rs:252), so two instances of config "claude" would both
   register as `claude` — colliding in the agent registry and advisory locks. The
   guard is what currently masks this.

There's even an internal contradiction: DESIGN S6.6 *claims* a project can carry "two
Claude instances both spawned from agent tool #3," while S10 + the code enforce one.

**Decisions made with the user:**
- **Both `spawn_agent` and `process_start` become pure factories** — drop the 1:1 guard
  entirely. Every call creates a fresh instance. "Focus the existing one" becomes a
  cockpit/UI concern, out of scope here.
- **Per-instance identity is uniquified**: internal `name` → `claude-191` (drives the
  registry/lock key); friendly `display_name` → `claude #191` (cockpit label).

**Outcome:** one agent tool spawns N independent, individually-addressable instances
that don't collide in the registry or locks — adding a sub-agent costs one `spawn_agent`
call, not a new config.

## Changes

### 1. Remove the guard + uniquify identity — `crates/panopt-core/src/state.rs`

In `process_start_with` (~1290-1357):

- **Delete the 1:1 guard** (lines 1303-1314): the whole
  `if let Some(existing) = …find(…) { return Ok(existing); }` block.
- **Uniquify name/display in the daemon at spawn**, solving the id-ordering by computing
  the strings *inside the existing transaction* after `let next = next_id(&tx, pid)?`
  (line 1328) and before the INSERT — no second UPDATE, single tx, uses `next_id` (never
  `MAX(id)`, per the shared-counter invariant). Bind the computed values in place of
  `config.name` (line 1338) and the `display_name` local (line 1339):
  - **internal `name`** (drives `agent_id`): `format!("{}-{next}", config.name)`, or
    `format!("agent-{next}")` when `config.name` is blank (matches the edge fallback at
    process.rs:256 and the handler ad-hoc convention at handler.rs:1528). Guarantees a
    unique, non-empty registry/lock key per instance.
  - **`display_name`** (friendly): `friendly = <per-launch name override if non-blank
    else config.display_name>`; result = `format!("{friendly} #{next}")`, falling back
    to the internal `name` when `friendly` is blank (so we never emit a bare `" #191"`).
    The per-launch `name` override is **suffixed too** (so two spawns with the same
    explicit `name="Reviewer"` still render `Reviewer #191` / `Reviewer #192`).
- The edge (`exec_agent_instance`) needs **no change** — it already reads `name` /
  `display_name` off the row (process.rs:252,257).

### 2. Rewrite stale doc comments — `crates/panopt-core/src/state.rs`

- `process_start` doc (1257-1269) and `process_start_with` doc (1278-1289): drop all
  "one live instance per config" / "focus the existing one" / "overrides are ignored"
  language; state pure-factory semantics + the `#N` uniquification.
- Inline comment 1316-1318: describe the new name/display uniquification.
- `reap_dead` doc (~line 470): remove the stale "the 1:1 policy keeps handing the zombie
  back" clause; keep the rest (reaping still stops dead rows being reported live).

### 3. Reconcile design docs — `DESIGN.md`

- **S6.6** (~525-585): keep the "one tool backs many instances" language; fix line ~548
  ("even at today's one-instance-per-config" is now false); optionally note identity is
  uniquified (`{name}-{id}` / `{friendly} #{id}`).
- **S10** (~750-755): rewrite the spawn bullet — remove "same one-live-instance-per-config
  policy"; state both `spawn_agent` and `process_start` are pure factories, instances
  uniquified by `#N`, focus-existing is a cockpit/UI concern. Keep return-shape and
  per-launch-override text.
- `HANDOFF.md`: no references found; re-check at edit time.

### 4. Tests — `crates/panopt-core/src/state.rs` test module

**Update (these assert the old 1:1 / un-suffixed display):**
- `process_start_report_stop_lifecycle` (~3674-3738): invert the "second start returns
  same row" assertions (3707-3710) → distinct id, `process_list().len() == 2`, both live.
  Fix the `display_name == "Mediator"` assertion (3701) → `"Mediator #{id}"`; add an
  internal-name assertion (`"claude-a-{id}"`).
- `process_start_with_records_overrides_without_mutating_the_config` (~3740-3789): fix the
  two `display_name` assertions (3768, 3784) to the suffixed form; the `assert_ne!` ids and
  per-instance `extra_args` assertions stay valid.
- `render_agent_instructions_substitutes_real_process_facts` (~3791-3830): the agent-id
  now contains `mediator-1-{id}` — the `contains("mediator-1")` substring still passes;
  glance at `render_agent_instructions` (~1369) to confirm which field it sources.

**Add:**
- `process_start_is_a_factory_distinct_instances`: spawn one config twice without stopping
  → two distinct ids, both live, `len()==2`, distinct internal names + display names, same
  `agent_tool_id`. (Core 1:N + anti-collision proof.)
- `process_start_empty_config_name_falls_back_to_agent_id`: empty `name`+`display_name` →
  row `name == display_name == "agent-{id}"` (no bare `#id`, no empty agent_id).
- `process_start_with_name_override_is_suffixed`: two spawns with the same `name="Reviewer"`
  → `"Reviewer #{id1}"` / `"Reviewer #{id2}"`.

## Verification

- `cargo check -p panopt-core -p panoptd -p panopt`
- `cargo clippy -p panopt-core -p panoptd -p panopt` (clippy is `-D warnings`)
- `cargo test -p panopt-core` (updated + new tests), `cargo test -p panoptd`
- Run the **`verify-all`** skill for the full workspace + WASM plugin sweep.
- **End-to-end MCP:** `just stop && just up` (fresh daemon, since daemon code changed) →
  pick/create an enabled config → call `process_start` (and `spawn_agent`) twice with the
  same `agent_tool_id` → `process_list` shows two rows: distinct `id`, both `starting`/
  `running`, same `agent_tool_id`, distinct `name` (`…-N1`/`…-N2`) and `display_name`
  (`… #N1`/`… #N2`). Optionally `process_report` distinct pids and confirm `agent_list`
  shows two distinct registry entries (the collision fix) and `.panopt/processes.md`
  lists both.

## Risks / notes

- **No focus-or-start dependents**: CLI `panopt process start` (process.rs:142) and the
  zellij plugin (`spawn_agent_pane`, legacy `panopt _agent` path) don't rely on the guard.
- **spawn_agent ad-hoc path** (handler.rs:1504-1542) already uniquifies the *config* name;
  removing the guard doesn't break it.
- **`processes.md` projection**: the `#N` suffix now appears in `display_name` — eyeball
  `reproject_processes` output so it reads cleanly.
- Scope is panopt-core + docs + a CLI/plugin glance; no schema migration needed (the
  schema already supports 1:N).

## panopt
PANopt coordination daemon: shared todos and notes across agents.
Each connection is scoped to one project by the ?ws=<project path> query parameter on the server URL.
- Registry: call identify (name, optional status) on startup so others can see you; whoami returns your own entry; agent_list returns every agent on the project (each entry's key_source is `declared` for stable `?agent=<id>` ids or `session` for the rotating MCP session id - only session entries idle-prune). Connecting already registers you. agent_leave removes your registry entry and releases your locks; the idle sweep handles agents that just disappear.
- Locks: lock_acquire (name, optional note) takes a named advisory lock and is non-blocking; lock_release frees it; lock_status lists every held lock. Locks are advisory - agents cooperate, the daemon does not enforce.
- Todos: todo_create (returns an id), todo_list (summaries), todo_get (one todo in full), todo_update (edit any field), todo_complete, todo_delete, todo_add_blocker / todo_remove_blocker / todo_set_blockers, todo_comment_add / todo_comment_update / todo_comment_delete, todo_tags_list (project tag vocabulary, union with notes), and todo_lock / todo_unlock (advisory `todo:<id>` lock, surfaced as locked_by on todo_get). Each todo also projects to .panopt/todos/<id>.md.
- Notes: note_create (returns an id), note_list, note_get (one note in full), note_append (add to body), note_read (body only), note_update (replace title, body, and/or tags), note_delete, note_tags_list (project tag vocabulary, same union as todo_tags_list). Each note also projects to .panopt/note/<id>.md.
- Agent tools (config layer): agent_tool_create (returns an id), agent_tool_list, agent_tool_get, agent_tool_update, agent_tool_delete. Durable per-project agent configurations the cockpit can spawn from. Projected to .panopt/agent_tools.md.
- Processes (instance layer): process_create (kind agent/command/terminal, optional agent_tool_id, returns an id), process_list, process_get, process_update, process_delete. Per-p… [truncated]

1490	    /// pre-made slot. An opening `prompt` is queued as the instance's first
1491	    /// input, delivered into its pane by the cockpit once it is live.

1500	
1501	            // Resolve the backing config: an existing one, or a fresh ad-hoc
1502	            // slot. Auto-creating a config keeps ad-hoc spawns inside the
1503	            // two-layer model - the agent shows up in the cockpit and reuses the
1504	            // whole config -> instance -> profile-render pipeline.
1505	            let tool_id = match args.agent_tool_id {
1506	                Some(id) => id,
1507	                None => {
1508	                    let tool_type = args
1509	                        .tool_type
1510	                        .clone()
1511	                        .unwrap_or_else(|| panopt_core::agent_profiles::DEFAULT_PROFILE_KEY.to_string());
1512	                    let label = args.name.clone().unwrap_or_default();
1513	                    let created = st
1514	                        .agent_tool_create(
1515	                            project,
1516	                            label.clone(),
1517	                            label.clone(),
1518	                            String::new(),
1519	                            String::new(),
1520	                            tool_type,
1521	                            String::new(),
1522	                            true,
1523	                        )
1524	                        .map_err(map_core_err)?;
1525	                    // With no name given, stamp a unique one so the registry
1526	                    // agent id (derived from the config name) can't collide with
1527	                    // another nameless ad-hoc spawn.
1528	                    if label.trim().is_empty() {
1529	                        let nm = format!("agent-{created}");
1530	                        st.agent_tool_update(
1531	                            project,
1532	                            created,
1533	                            AgentToolPatch {

1537	                            },

1542	                }
1543	            };

#205 done. Here's what shipped — the answer to "it deleted the agent but not the config" implemented as policy.

## What changed

**Policy: ad-hoc = disposable, declared = durable.** An ad-hoc `spawn_agent` (no `agent_tool_id`) now mints its backing config flagged `ephemeral`; `process_delete` reaps that config the moment its *last* live instance is gone. Configs you create explicitly (`agent_tool_create`, or spawn by `agent_tool_id`) are durable templates and are never auto-reaped.

**Schema** (`db.rs`) — V17: `ephemeral INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` on `agent_tools`, forward-only, `add_column_if_missing` (dev-drift safe). Existing configs read back as durable.

**Core** (`model.rs`, `state.rs`):
- `AgentTool.ephemeral` + `AgentToolPatch.ephemeral`; read paths (`agent_tool_list`/`fetch_agent_tool`) and `agent_tool_update` SET carry it.
- `process_delete` captures the backing `agent_tool_id` before the soft-delete, then calls a new `reap_ephemeral_config(project, tool_id)` helper: reaps **only** if the config is `ephemeral` *and* has zero remaining live instances (the just-deleted one is already excluded). Re-projects `agent_tools.md` only when it actually reaps.

**Daemon** (`handler.rs`): the ad-hoc spawn path sets `ephemeral: Some(true)` (folded into the same post-create `agent_tool_update` that already uniquifies a nameless config — one update, not two). `AgentToolDto` surfaces `ephemeral` for `agent_tool_get`/`list`. Disposal etiquette in the server instructions updated.

**Docs**: `DESIGN.md` S6.6 (lifecycle split of the config layer) and S10 (Dispose) note the ephemeral reap.

I kept `agent_tool_create`'s signature untouched (it always makes a durable config), so the new flag is set via the patch — that avoided churning ~20 test call sites and keeps the diff focused on the actual change.

**Tests** (+3): V17 default-column migration test; `process_delete_does_not_reap_a_durable_config`; `process_delete_reaps_an_ephemeral_config_with_its_last_instance` (proves the config survives while a sibling is live, then vanishes with the last instance).

I haven't committed — say `cnp` and I'll stack it. This also unblocks **#206** (the idle-TTL sweep keys off this `ephemeral` flag). Still outstanding from the earlier batch: **#207** (suppress, don't strand, the pane on disposal) and **#208** (live re-verify the full orchestration runtime after `just refresh`).

Spawned agents persist (a config can fan out N instances since the 1:N factory change, todo #190). On 2026-06-07 the user chose the cleanup model: **caller-driven disposal + opt-in ephemeral TTL** (not pure-manual, not aggressive idle auto-reap — an idle-but-live Claude Code agent is expensive context and must NOT be auto-killed unless explicitly spawned ephemeral).

**Why:** matches soloterm's caller-driven discipline (stop_process vs close_process, no auto-reap) while adding a safety valve for one-shot fan-out. panopt's existing primitives: `process_stop` (→STOPPED, no resume — `process_start` now spawns fresh), `process_delete` (soft), `sweep_dead_processes` (running→EXITED on dead pid), `sweep_idle_agents` (prunes *registry* entry + locks at 30m, leaves the process row + pane). Never-close-panes invariant means disposal must *suppress* panes, not close them.

**How to apply (implementation status):**
- **A — disposal etiquette (DONE):** `spawn_agent` tool description + daemon server `instructions` (handler.rs get_info) now say agents persist until disposed and to `process_stop` then `process_delete` what you spawn.
- **B — pending:** schema V17 `ephemeral` col on `agent_tools`; ad-hoc `spawn_agent` sets it; `process_delete` reaps the ephemeral config when its last live instance goes (fixes ad-hoc spawns minting a permanent config each call).
- **C — pending:** plugin suppresses (not closes) the pane when a process leaves the live set.
- **D — pending:** `SpawnAgentArgs.ephemeral`; new daemon `sweep_ephemeral_idle` reaps ephemeral + RUNNING + idle (agent_state/state_since from #142/#143) past a TTL. Order: B→D→C.

Related: [[rebuild-runtime-artifacts]] (must `just refresh` to test daemon/plugin changes).

Keying the idle-sweep off the same `ephemeral` flag would auto-kill every ad-hoc agent — wrong. So D needs a **separate, per-instance opt-in**. Let me study the sweep machinery before deciding:

input.new_string:
not strand an orphaned config. Configs you spawn from explicitly (by `agent_tool_id`,
  or created via `agent_tool_create`) are durable templates and are never auto-reaped.
  - *Opt-in idle auto-reap (V18, todo #206).* A spawn may pass `idle_ttl_secs`; the
    daemon's idle sweep then stops + deletes that instance once it has sat `idle`
    (by `agent_state`/`state_since`) past the TTL. The TTL lives on the instance,
    not the config, and the sweep keys off it - **not** the `ephemeral` flag - so
    auto-kill is strictly opt-in: an instance with no TTL (the default) is never
    touched, honoring the rule that an idle-but-live agent is expensive context and
    must not be auto-killed unless asked.
  - *Pane suppression (todo #207).* `process_stop`/`process_delete` only change the
    daemon record; the cockpit plugin reconciles the disposal by **suppressing** the
    now-dead agent pane (swap a viewer over it - hidden, not closed, per the
    never-close invariant), the mirror of how it reconciles a `starting` row into a
    pane. So disposing a sub-agent over MCP sheds its husk from the cockpit.

`project_id` cross-project spawn is a deferred non-goal

A fire-and-forget sub-agent can now opt into self-disposal: spawn_agent takes
idle_ttl_secs, recorded on the instance, and the daemon's idle sweep stops +
deletes the instance once it has sat idle past the TTL (then reaps an ephemeral
backing config via #205). Strictly opt-in - the sweep keys off the per-instance
TTL, NOT the config ephemeral flag, so an idle-but-live agent with no TTL is
never auto-killed (expensive-context constraint).

- db.rs: V18 adds processes.idle_ttl_secs (nullable, NULL = never reap).
- model.rs: Process.idle_ttl_secs + ProcessPatch.idle_ttl_secs.
- state.rs: read/update paths carry it; new sweep_idle_ttl (running + idle +
  ttl set + now-state_since >= ttl -> process_stop then process_delete),
  returning pids for the host to signal.
- params.rs/lib.rs: SpawnAgentArgs.idle_ttl_secs + tool-description updates.
- handler.rs: spawn_agent records the TTL; ProcessDto surfaces it;
  signal_terminate is pub(crate); server instructions mention the opt-in.
- main.rs: 15s daemon timer runs sweep_idle_ttl and SIGTERMs reaped pids.
- DESIGN.md S10: document opt-in idle auto-reap.
